question: Conveying clinical urgency on an imaging requisition — for example labelling a scan 'STAT' or 'within 4 hours' — is primarily intended to ensure the radiologist prioritises writing the report rather than to influence when the scan is actually performed.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Urgency labelling primarily determines when the scan is performed (scanner scheduling). It also accelerates reporting, but a correct urgency tier is essential so that the scan is not delayed behind routine cases while a deteriorating patient waits.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Actually, this is false. Urgency labelling drives both scanner scheduling and report turnaround. Its primary function is to ensure the patient is moved to the front of the queue for the scan itself; report prioritisation follows from that. Under-communicating urgency delays the scan, not just the report.
